about.title: Pleasanton Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: Pleasanton's economy runs on office parks along the I-580 corridor, distribution warehouses, hotels, retail, and the trades that keep all of it built and maintained. When someone gets hurt doing that work, the first system they meet is California workers' compensation. It pays for medical care and partial wage replacement whether or not anyone was at fault, and in most cases it is the only claim you can bring against your own employer. What many injured workers in Alameda County never hear is that a second door may exist. If a subcontractor, a property owner, an equipment manufacturer, or another driver caused the harm, a separate injury claim against that third party can reach losses workers' comp leaves out, like full lost wages and pain and suffering. Driving is a good example. Pleasanton recorded 324 injury collisions in 2025, with 447 people hurt and 3 deaths, and some of those crashes involved people on the clock along I-580 and I-680. LawProactive is a free connection service, not a law firm. We match you with an independent attorney who can look at both paths and explain which ones apply to you.

items.question: I was rear-ended on I-580 while driving for my Pleasanton employer. Is workers' comp all I get?
items.answer: Not necessarily. Workers' comp should cover your medical bills and part of your wages because you were working at the time, but the other driver is a third party, and California allows a separate injury claim against a negligent third party. That claim can include losses workers' comp does not pay, and it generally must be filed within two years. An independent attorney can review the crash report and tell you whether both claims make sense.

items.question: My supervisor hinted I should not file a report. What happens if I do anyway?
items.answer: Reporting a workplace injury is your right, and California law makes it illegal for an employer to retaliate against you for doing so. You should report within 30 days to protect your workers' compensation benefits. If you face demotion, cut hours, or termination after reporting, tell the attorney you are connected with, because that conduct can be addressed separately.
